SMTO-SKL-0128 — Slack couldn't find that conversation thread

GUID: cefcd786-e3a8-58df-9b3d-6c1bf42f906b
Slug: slack-thread-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • SMTO asked Slack for a thread by its first message, but Slack couldn't find that thread in the channel. Nothing was posted or changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to show recent messages in the channel and choose the message that starts the thread. A thread is found by the exact posting time of its first message; a reply's time won't work.
  2. Check in Slack that the thread's first message still exists and is in the same channel. If the first message was deleted or is in another channel, Slack can't find the thread.
  3. Ask the Agent for your request again using that thread. Slack didn't act on the first request, so it's safe to repeat.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reads or replies in the thread you meant.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with a link to the thread copied from Slack, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack returned thread_not_found for the supplied channel_id and parent thread_ts.

What this means

  • Slack returns the thread_not_found API reason. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack returns the thread_not_found API reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify exact channel_id and parent thread_ts from retained or bounded history evidence.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the parent thread_ts (the thread's root message ts, not a reply ts) with a bounded slack.history read of the exact channel_id, then call slack.thread or slack.reply with that value.
  • Verify the exact channel_id and parent thread_ts with a bounded history read.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended visible thread is read by its exact parent timestamp.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
